intro: You have arrived at Parium, an ancient city in Çanakkale province, with a story spanning the 7th century BC to the 13th century AD. It was a Greek harbour city on the Troad coast of the Sea of Marmara, and it was famed for two things: its odeon and its coinage.
history: Parium was founded in the 7th century BC by colonists from Paros, Thasos and Erythrae. It prospered thanks to its strategic harbour at the southern entrance to the straits. Under Rome and Byzantium it was an important bishopric, until it was abandoned in the 13th century.
structure-6: You are now at the City Gate, a monumental gateway in the city walls. Imagine everyone who once passed through it, coming up from the harbour.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Odeon, the Roman Bath, the Necropolis, the Theatre and the Agora.
facts: Did you know? Parium won the status of a Roman colony and struck its own coins, marked with a Gorgon's head. Its hemidrachms bearing the Gorgon are among the best-known coins of the ancient world. Thousands of graves have been excavated in its necropolis, making it one of Anatolia's richest records of Roman burial custom.
outro: This brings our tour of Parium to an end. Before you go, please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. This harbour city has waited for centuries; let it keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
